newsitem.title: USA: D&P assigns initial ratings to Revlon debt.
newsitem.headline: D&P assigns initial ratings to Revlon debt.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it has assigned initial ratings of double B to Revlon Consumer Products Corp's $600 million senior secured bank credit facilities.

D&P also rated its $85 million senior secured sinking fund debentures, single-B-plus; its $200 million and $260 million senior unsecured notes, single-B; and its $555 million senior subordinated debt, single-B-minus.
Revlon Consumer Products is a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Revlon Inc, which is in turn a direct majority-owned subsidiary of Revlon Worldwide.
These actions affect about $2.4 billion of outstanding debt at Revlon Consumer Products and Revlon Worldwide.
D&P said it has also assigned an initial rating of single-B-minus to Revlon Worldwide Corp's $1.1 billion senior secured discount debt.
Revlon Inc completed an initial public offering in March 1996 and contributed $187.8 million to Revlon Consumer Products to repay outstanding bank debt.

The debt ratings are based on Revlon's strong market position, global brand name recognition and improving operating performance, D&P said. These factors are offset by high debt levels at both Revlon Consumer Products and Revlon Worldwide, the rating company said in a statement.
